guide.summary: Museums, churches, a river cruise and family stops in Galway, with breakfast cafés, bakeries, dinners and music bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Galway City Museum is closed on Mondays and the Corrib Princess does not sail on Mondays, so save Monday for St Nicholas' Collegiate Church, Galway Cathedral and the Atlantaquaria, which all publish Monday opening.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Galway City Museum opens Tuesday to Saturday, and the Corrib Princess is closed on Mondays. Aniar is closed on Sunday and Monday, and Ard Bia at Nimmos serves dinner Tuesday to Sunday.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Galway City Museum is free with no booking required, and the Galway Civic Trust's free weekly tours from the Hall of the Red Earl recommend booking. Corrib Princess online booking opens one month in advance.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: The Dáil Bar serves bar food from 12pm with no reservation needed. Aniar and Cava Bodega ask you to phone to check availability.

toolkit.label: Visitor rules
toolkit.copy: Galway Cathedral asks visitors not to enter during Mass unless taking part and suggests a €3 donation. St Nicholas' Collegiate Church has last entry 30 minutes before closing, and the Atlantaquaria's last admission is one hour before closing.

guide.dek: Anchor your days on the free museum and medieval church in the old centre, then book dinner around Monday and Sunday closures.
intro: Galway's old centre is compact, and several of its main sights cost nothing to enter. Galway City Museum on Spanish Parade charges no admission and needs no booking; it opens Tuesday to Saturday from 10am to 5pm, adds Sunday afternoons from Easter to mid-September, and its galleries close at 4:45pm. Current displays include The Claddagh, A Triumph of Unconscious Beauty and Revolution in Galway, 1913 - 1923. A short walk away on Lombard Street, St Nicholas' Collegiate Church opens every day, from 11am on Wednesdays and 1pm on Sundays, with last entry 30 minutes before closing.

For a guided start, the Galway Civic Trust runs free weekly tours from the Hall of the Red Earl on Druid Lane; booking is not required but is recommended, and its Churches of Galway tour runs every Thursday at 12pm. Galway Cathedral is usually open from 8am to 8pm, asks you not to enter during Mass unless you are taking part, and suggests a €3 donation. On the river, the Corrib Princess leaves from Waterside, Woodquay, for 90-minute guided trips; it does not sail on Mondays, and online booking opens one month in advance.

Plan dinners around closing days. Aniar on Lower Dominick Street serves a tasting menu from Tuesday to Saturday and is closed on Sunday and Monday, while Ard Bia at Nimmos beside the Spanish Arch serves dinner Tuesday to Sunday and weekend brunch from 10am to 3pm. Brasserie on the Corner on Eglinton Street opens daily from 10am with last orders at 9.30pm, and Cava Bodega on Middle Street, with more than 70 Spanish tapas, asks you to phone to check availability. For breakfast, Urban Grind on William Street West serves brunch seven days a week until 3pm.

Evenings bring live music. The Dáil Bar on Middle Street has music every night from 9:30pm and serves bar food from 12pm with no reservation needed, and O'Connor's Bar in Salthill lists traditional Irish music Monday to Friday. Tigh Neachtain on Cross Street serves lunch from 12pm to 4pm. With children, Galway Atlantaquaria on Seapoint Promenade opens daily, with last admission an hour before closing, and the council's Millennium Children's Park Playground on University Road is open from 7am to 7pm daily for ages 1 to 12.
summaryCards: Pair the free Galway City Museum on Spanish Parade with St Nicholas' Collegiate Church on Lombard Street, then take a Corrib Princess trip from Woodquay on any day except Monday.
Start with brunch at Urban Grind on William Street West or a pastry at Gourmet Tart Co. on Lower Abbeygate Street, which opens at 7am Monday to Saturday.
Aniar is closed on Sunday and Monday and takes bookings by phone, and Corrib Princess online booking opens only one month ahead.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several well-known Galway venues could not be read: The King's Head, Coffeewerk + Press, Sheridans Cheesemongers, McCambridge's, Rúibín, Monroe's, The Dough Bros and Hazel Mountain Chocolate returned rate-limit errors; Griffin's Bakery, Dela, Tartare and the Town Hall Theatre refused automated reading; The Crane Bar, Cupán Tae and Geometry Coffee failed on certificate errors; none of these failures is evidence of closure. Public areas such as the Latin Quarter and Salthill Promenade have no operator page and were not checked. Hours were not published for the Hall of the Red Earl, Sophie's at The Dean, Quincentennial Park and the University of Galway, Corrib Princess sailing times were not on its home page, Galway Cathedral's hours are described as approximate, and Gourmet Tart Co.'s Abbeygate Street Sunday hours appear to contain a typo. Galway City Council posted storm reopening notices on 25 and 27 October 2026 without naming the locations, so check outdoor sites on the day. Several confirmations (Ard Bia, Corrib Princess, Tigh Neachtain, O'Connor's Bar, Cava Bodega) rest on published hours or booking tools rather than dated 2026 content.
